name: Shringasaurus
notes: Horned archosauromorph of the Denwa ground, not a dinosaur and not a crocodile -- an older diapsid branch that outlasted both here. A pair of forward-curving horns sits above the eyes, on adults only; yearlings are hornless and are often taken for something else entirely. Browses the high branches by rearing onto its hind legs, which is what the neck is for.
journal_prompt: Two horns come up out of the scrub before the head does, curved forward like a bull's and set above the eyes rather than on the nose. The animal rears slowly against a tree, takes what it came for, and drops back down.
